tasks.short: Maintain customer relationships and resolve payment, billing, and financial service problems.

steps.what: Check customer balances, invoices, and payment terms in the {ERP}.
Read the customer complaint and correspondence in the {EMAIL}.

loop.input: Selected customer correspondence, complaint, and account summary.
loop.output: Issue brief with requests, disputed facts, deadlines, and source references.
loop.check: Require source references; verify amounts against the account summary; flag conflicting statements.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per case; unresolved conflicts return to manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Customer requests and explanations arrive as free text with inconsistent wording.

steps.what: Discuss the problem, understand constraints, and rebuild trust with the customer.
Decide a settlement or payment arrangement within delegated authority.
Draft the agreed explanation, terms, and next steps in the {EMAIL}.

loop.input: Approved resolution decision and discussion notes.
loop.output: Customer reply draft stating approved terms and next steps.
loop.check: Compare amounts, dates, and commitments with the resolution decision; flag unsupported promises.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; failed checks return to manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: The explanation must address the customer's specific concerns in natural language.

steps.what: Approve and send the customer reply through the {EMAIL}.
Record the outcome and follow-up date in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: An integration retrieves the account summary from the {ERP}; bounded loops turn selected {EMAIL} correspondence into a sourced issue brief and reply draft. The finance manager conducts the conversation and authorises commitments before sending, while configured {CRM} workflows record the outcome and follow-up.
tasks.previous_blocker: Account facts and correspondence are separated. Relationship repair and settlement decisions require personal judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing interfaces support account retrieval and activity logging. AI-assisted coding can reduce integration effort, and bounded loops can prepare sourced summaries.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed facts, unusual contracts, and distressed customers need attention. Larger concessions require escalation under the approval policy.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising unspoken concerns, rebuilding trust, and choosing a commercially fair resolution.

ambition.what: Early payment-difficulty conversations for smaller business customers.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less account reconstruction and more customer problem solving. Settlement authority remains defined by the existing delegation.

reach.task: Arrange realistic payment plans for overdue accounts.
reach.learn: Learn collection stages, affordability questions, and escalation thresholds.

reach.task: Assess whether revised payment terms increase credit exposure.
reach.learn: Learn credit-limit logic and how disputed invoices affect exposure.

evidence.claim: Account retrieval, approved correspondence, and activity logging can use deterministic integrations and configured workflows.
Free-text summaries and replies need source checks and human review before customer commitments.

assumptions: This task concerns corporate customer accounts and disputes rather than regulated investment advice.
The company uses the {CRM} for customer activity and the {ERP} for account balances.
Time shares are estimates of task effort, with relationship work remaining dominant.
Build ranges estimate a limited pilot; access and any consultation under national rules can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which customer records and correspondence the finance manager may access.
Whether the {ERP} and {CRM} expose suitable interfaces.
Settlement limits and escalation roles.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the proposed processing.
research_questions: Do issue briefs preserve disputed facts and customer intent?
Can existing {CRM} configuration capture approved correspondence without custom code?
new_work: Review issue briefs and reply drafts.
Resolve conflicting records and failed account matches.
Maintain templates, access permissions, and integration mappings.
tasks.statement: Establish and maintain relationships with individual or business customers or provide assistance with problems these customers may encounter.

tasks.short: Direct finance-team workloads, resolve operational priorities, and coach employees.

steps.what: Review overdue finance work and control exceptions in the {ERP}.
Prepare a team capacity and deadline plan in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Choose priorities, responsibilities, and escalation routes in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Discuss dependencies, obstacles, and responsibilities with the finance team.
Coach individual employees on difficult work and development needs.
Record agreed owners, dates, and escalations in the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: Configured {ERP} reports expose overdue work and control exceptions; deterministic calculations create a team capacity plan from deadlines and declared availability. The finance manager assigns people and handles coaching, while configured {PROJECT} workflows record approved assignments and send reminders.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finance queues and team planning are separate. Informal dependencies and personal circumstances make fully automatic assignment unsuitable.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting and work-management configuration can handle much of the task. Small integrations and capacity calculations are easier to build and maintain with AI-assisted coding.
tasks.still_hard: Skill coverage, segregation of duties, development needs, and competing deadlines require judgement. Employee-data processing needs GDPR assessment and consultation where national rules apply; later AI-based allocation would also need EU AI Act assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding capability and motivation, handling conflict, and developing people while protecting financial controls.

ambition.what: A weekly close-capacity decision before deadline pressure becomes overtime.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less status collection and more coaching and early capacity decisions. The manager retains existing assignment rights; staffing and pay changes still need their established approvals.

reach.task: Compare temporary staffing costs with the cost of delayed finance work.
reach.learn: Learn capacity-cost scenarios and budget approval limits.

reach.task: Define useful process backlog and deadline metrics.
reach.learn: Learn metric definitions, refresh checks, and misleading workload proxies.

evidence.claim: Deadline arithmetic, team capacity summaries, approved assignment recording, and reminders can use deterministic technology.
Process workload measures cannot alone determine individual capability, development needs, or fair assignments.

assumptions: The finance manager leads a corporate finance team rather than a financial-services branch.
A spreadsheet currently bridges operational reporting and team planning.
Capacity calculations use declared availability and process demand; the manager assigns individual employees.
Build ranges estimate a pilot; national consultation processes may take longer.
unknowns: Which queues, deadlines, and assignments are already available in existing systems.
Team size, skill coverage, and segregation-of-duties requirements.
Whether recording availability introduces new employee-data processing.
Applicable national consultation requirements and existing employee agreements.
research_questions: Can configured reports replace manual status collection without new monitoring?
Which capacity measures predict bottlenecks without becoming individual performance scores?
new_work: Maintain task dependencies, capacity assumptions, and control constraints.
Correct missing queue records and stale availability.
Review access permissions and whether metrics create unintended incentives.
tasks.statement: Plan, direct, or coordinate the activities of workers in branches, offices, or departments of establishments, such as branch banks, brokerage firms, risk and insurance departments, or credit departments.

tasks.short: Define finance vacancies, assess candidates, and coordinate hiring with recruitment and human resources.

steps.what: Define responsibilities, essential criteria, and the role brief in the {DOCS}.
Approve the vacancy scope and funding through the {WORKFLOW}.
Create and publish the approved vacancy through the {ATS}.
Review applications against essential criteria in the {ATS}.
Arrange interviews using the {CALENDAR}.
Interview candidates and discuss relevant work examples.
Record the hiring decision and reasons in the {ATS}.
Prepare the offer from approved templates in the {DOCS}.
Approve terms and issue the offer through the {ESIGN}.

tasks.design: Approved role templates in the {DOCS} feed vacancy approval in the {WORKFLOW} and publication in the {ATS}. Configured {CALENDAR} scheduling and offer generation remove coordination work, while people assess candidates and approve offers before release through the {ESIGN}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Role definitions, vacancy approvals, scheduling, and offer paperwork cross several teams. Existing features may be only partly configured.
tasks.enabler_now: Templates, approval routing, scheduling, and document merging are established capabilities. AI-assisted coding can make small gaps between systems cheaper to close.
tasks.still_hard: Assessing evidence fairly, agreeing requirements, and attracting candidates remain human work. GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; any later AI candidate scoring needs separate assessment, and national rules may require consultation.
tasks.human_edge: Testing finance judgement, understanding motivation, and making a defensible hiring decision through direct interaction.

ambition.what: Career changers assessed through finance work examples and transferable skills.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time arranging interviews and assembling documents, with more time for candidate assessment. Hiring and pay approval rights follow the existing delegation.

reach.task: Design realistic work examples for assessing accounting and control judgement.
reach.learn: Learn which examples reveal competence and how to score evidence consistently.

reach.task: Review recruitment records and the proposed use of candidate data.
reach.learn: Learn retention limits, meaningful human review, and applicable national requirements.

evidence.claim: Vacancy approvals, scheduling, offer templates, and signature routing can largely use existing software configuration.
Candidate assessment and selection require meaningful human judgement in this design.

assumptions: The finance manager acts as hiring manager, supported by recruitment and human resources.
The company has approved role and offer templates and uses the listed system slots.
Scheduling uses approved shortlists and agreed availability.
The design introduces no automated candidate ranking or rejection.
Build ranges estimate a pilot; consultation and access waits may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Existing scheduling, document-generation, and approval capabilities.
Who approves vacancies, offers, and exceptions to pay bands.
Candidate-data retention rules and access permissions.
Applicable national consultation requirements.
Whether work-example assessment is suitable for the roles being recruited.
research_questions: Which administrative features can be enabled without custom integration?
Do essential criteria exclude career changers without a clear job-related reason?
Can interview evidence support consistent selection reasons across candidates?
new_work: Maintain role criteria, interview guides, and offer templates.
Handle scheduling exceptions and failed signature routing.
Review permissions, retention settings, and selection records.

tasks.short: Prepare operational and financial risk reports for management review.

steps.what: Export period balances, cash positions, and operational indicators.
Reconcile totals, align reporting periods, and calculate variances.
Collect explanations of unusual movements and emerging operational risks.

loop.input: Owner explanations linked to specified reporting exceptions.
loop.output: Attributed risk notes and a list of unresolved questions.
loop.check: Require source references; separate reported explanations from verified facts.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per reporting batch; unanswered questions return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Operational explanations arrive as varied free text and contain qualifications.

steps.what: Decide which movements and risks require management attention.
Assemble report tables, charts, commentary, and proposed management actions.

loop.input: Validated tables, selected material issues, and attributed risk notes.
loop.output: Report commentary linked to deterministically generated tables and charts.
loop.check: Check every number against table fields; reject unsupported causes and unapproved proposed actions.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair; failed checks produce a tables-only report with commentary gaps.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables use templates, but explaining changing risks requires bounded prose generation.

steps.what: Review accuracy, challenge conclusions, and authorise report release.
Distribute the approved report to the management audience.

tasks.design: Scheduled inputs from the {ERP}, {BANK}, and {OPS_SYSTEM} feed reconciled reporting tables on the {DATA_PLATFORM}, with charts in {BI}. Bounded loops extract attributed explanations and draft commentary from validated figures and the manager's materiality assessment. The {WORKFLOW} releases the report through {DOCS} and {EMAIL} only after controller approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Period alignment, inconsistent definitions, and manual commentary collection made report assembly costly and fragile.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured exports and deterministic reporting pipelines handle the figures. Bounded text loops can organise explanations without calculating or deciding materiality.
tasks.still_hard: Late corrections, inconsistent operational definitions, and unsupported causal explanations still require investigation.
tasks.human_edge: The manager distinguishes a noisy variance from an emerging risk and frames the decision management actually needs to make.

ambition.what: A weekly liquidity-and-operating-risk exception review between monthly reporting cycles.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from report assembly toward exception investigation and management discussion. The manager can bring emerging issues forward sooner; risk acceptance and spending authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Define escalation triggers for liquidity and operating exposures.
reach.learn: Risk appetite, indicator limitations, and scenario interpretation.

reach.task: Maintain a traceable management-report dataset.
reach.learn: Period snapshots, data contracts, and lineage.

evidence.claim: Nomentia documents cash forecasting using bank and ERP data and comparison of forecast with actual; this supports the cash component only.
Reconciliation, variance calculation, charts, and report distribution can use deterministic rules; commentary and materiality require separate controls.

assumptions: The initial scope is an internal management report, not a statutory filing.
Report definitions and an approval route already exist.
Build estimates cover one report family and a limited set of source systems.
GDPR access and retention controls apply where extracts contain personal data.
Consent and access estimates include consultation under national rules if employee-level reporting changes require it.
unknowns: Which reports and risk categories are in scope?
Are balances provisional or closed when reports are prepared?
Who can approve release and who may receive each report?
Can operational data be reconciled to finance periods?
Is employee-level information necessary?
research_questions: Can existing reporting configuration replace custom table and chart generation?
What evidence threshold should commentary meet before a causal explanation is included?
How should restatements propagate to previously distributed reports?
new_work: Resolve failed reconciliations and late source corrections.
Review commentary and attribution.
Maintain report definitions, access lists, and approval routing.
Monitor whether more frequent reporting produces useful decisions.
tasks.statement: Prepare operational or risk reports for management analysis.

tasks.short: Evaluate costs, compare budget scenarios, and recommend spending plans.

steps.what: Extract actual costs and commitments by cost centre.
Combine costs, correct mappings, and calculate budget scenarios.
Assess cost drivers and select scenarios worth discussing.
Challenge assumptions and agree proposed spending tradeoffs.
Prepare the budget proposal and supporting tables.
Approve the spending plan and release the budget version.

tasks.design: Configure scheduled cost and commitment exports from the {ERP}; deterministic calculations on the {DATA_PLATFORM} feed scenario comparisons in the {BI}. A template generator produces the proposal in the {DOCS}, and the {WORKFLOW} releases the budget to the {ERP} after finance director approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cost mappings, assumptions, and proposal templates differed between teams. Connecting them required bespoke integration and repeated reconciliation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports and calculation libraries support this design. AI coding can reduce implementation effort, but no customer-specific speed multiplier is established.
tasks.still_hard: Allocations, unreliable commitments, and strategic spending tradeoffs still need financial judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a cheap option damages delivery, resilience, or future capacity.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling tables to testing cost assumptions with budget owners. The manager selects scenarios for more frequent review; existing spending approval limits remain.

reach.task: Build driver-based budget scenarios.
reach.learn: Learn sensitivity analysis, allocation methods, and how operating drivers become costs.

reach.task: Publish reconciled cost comparisons.
reach.learn: Learn data lineage, reconciliation checks, and access-controlled reporting.

evidence.claim: Structured cost aggregation, scenario calculations, and template generation can use deterministic technology.
Budget tradeoffs require managerial judgement even when calculations are automated.

assumptions: This is departmental budgeting in a mid-size European company.
Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured savings.
Build ranges cover one initial budgeting scope using existing system exports.
EU GDPR and EU AI Act applicability are assessed for the chosen data and use. Employee consultation follows national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Whether the {ERP} already provides usable budgeting and scenario functions.
The quality of cost centre mappings and commitment data.
Whether individual employee costs are needed or aggregated costs suffice.
The actual budget approval limits and access requirements.
research_questions: Can existing {ERP} configuration replace the proposed calculation layer?
Which cost drivers explain decisions better than historical line-item comparisons?
new_work: Resolve mapping and reconciliation exceptions.
Maintain scenario assumptions and proposal templates.
Check scheduled exports after accounting changes.
tasks.statement: Evaluate data pertaining to costs to plan budgets.

tasks.short: Set finance training priorities, coordinate delivery, and assess whether learning improves work.

steps.what: Review finance course completions and outstanding requirements.
Discuss skill gaps, workload constraints, and learning needs with team leads.
Write a training plan with courses, objectives, timing, and costs.

loop.input: Training needs, delivery constraints, approved course catalogue, and training budget.
loop.output: Draft training plan with course references and stated learning objectives.
loop.check: Validate course identifiers, dates, and costs deterministically; the manager checks suitability and objectives.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per plan; unresolved needs return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text learning needs require interpretation before matching them to courses and objectives.

steps.what: Approve the training plan and spending commitment.
Assign approved courses and schedule reminders.
Coordinate delivery, coach staff, and resolve attendance or learning barriers.
Assess learning outcomes against finance process quality.

tasks.design: Configure completion views, assignments, and reminders in the {LMS}. A bounded drafting loop prepares training plans in the {DOCS}, while the {WORKFLOW} records spending approval and the {BI} presents aggregate learning and process outcomes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Course administration was available, but team-specific needs and delivery constraints remained in conversations and documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing {LMS} functions handle administration. A bounded model loop can turn documented needs into a reviewable plan without assessing employees autonomously.
tasks.still_hard: Completion does not prove competence, and process improvements cannot easily be attributed to training.
tasks.human_edge: Notice hidden learning barriers and coach people without turning development into surveillance.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time chasing attendance and more time coaching finance teams through practical exercises. Training priorities stay within the existing budget and approval mandate.

reach.task: Design practical exercises for month-end close.
reach.learn: Learn close dependencies, common control failures, and ways to assess demonstrated competence.

reach.task: Translate recurring accounting errors into learning examples.
reach.learn: Learn how to distinguish skill gaps from unclear procedures or broken tools.

evidence.claim: Learning systems commonly support course assignments, completion records, and reminders.
Significant decisions about staff should not be made solely through automation where GDPR Article 22 applies.
Using AI to evaluate employee performance can bring the use within an employment high-risk category.

assumptions: The task concerns training for the finance team, rather than company-wide learning leadership.
The proposed loop drafts plans; it does not score employees or decide promotion, pay, or discipline.
Step shares and build ranges are estimates for one team and an existing {LMS}.
GDPR applies to learning records. EU AI Act classification depends on actual use; consultation follows national rules.
The consultation range is working effort and may not capture elapsed statutory or negotiation time.
unknowns: Available {LMS} configuration and integration permissions.
Whether employee representatives must be consulted under applicable national rules.
Whether learning data currently informs consequential employment decisions.
The finance team's training budget, course coverage, and delivery capacity.
research_questions: Which finance errors are caused by learning needs rather than process design?
Can aggregate process outcomes assess training without individual performance scoring?
new_work: Review drafted training plans and unsuitable course matches.
Resolve assignment and attendance exceptions.
Maintain the course catalogue and learning objectives.
Check access to employee learning records.

tasks.short: Process loan applications and prepare evidence-based credit assessments for authorised decision makers.

steps.what: Register the application and attach submitted evidence in the {OTHER} lending records system.
Read submitted documents and extract financial and applicant facts.

loop.input: Submitted financial statements, income evidence, application fields and evidence requirements.
loop.output: Proposed application fields with page references and explicit missing or conflicting values.
loop.check: Validate types, dates and arithmetic relationships; the analyst confirms material fields against source pages.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document; unreadable or conflicting evidence goes to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Use direct field imports where available; varied document layouts and prose need bounded extraction.

steps.what: Calculate repayment ratios, exposure and credit-policy flags.
Request missing or inconsistent evidence from the applicant.
Assess repayment prospects, evidence quality and policy exceptions.
Discuss material anomalies and proposed financing needs with the applicant.
Finalise the assessment and submit it through the {OTHER} lending records system.

tasks.design: Configure intake and evidence checklists in the {OTHER} lending records system, with documents in {DOCS}. A bounded extraction loop proposes sourced fields; deterministic calculations produce ratios and policy flags, and {WORKFLOW} prepares evidence requests for review. The credit analyst assesses repayment prospects and approves the assembled assessment before it enters the separate credit-approval process.
tasks.previous_blocker: Applicants supplied varied documents, and analysts retyped figures into separate calculation sheets. Exceptions and evidence requests were difficult to express as a single fixed form.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured intake removes avoidable rekeying, while bounded document extraction handles the remaining varied evidence. Calculations and completeness checks remain ordinary rules.
tasks.still_hard: Extracted facts do not establish authenticity or future repayment capacity. GDPR, the EU AI Act and national lending rules constrain personal-data use and any later move into automated creditworthiness assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguishing a weak document trail from a weak borrower and recognising explanations that require further corroboration.

ambition.what: A pre-application evidence-readiness checklist for small-business borrowers.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time transcribing documents and more time investigating repayment risks and speaking with applicants. The finance manager receives a more consistent assessment; final credit authority remains in the separate approval task.

reach.task: Investigate inconsistent application evidence.
reach.learn: Document provenance, corroboration and escalation thresholds.

reach.task: Prepare repayment-capacity assessments.
reach.learn: Cash-flow normalisation, debt-service calculations and policy exceptions.

evidence.claim: Document extraction can propose sourced fields while deterministic calculations handle ratios and completeness checks.
A human decision gate must provide meaningful review where significant natural-person decisions engage GDPR Article 22.
Loan processing is a specialist lending activity and is not normally part of ordinary corporate finance management.

assumptions: This task applies only where the company originates or administers loans.
The initial scope covers one loan product and a limited set of evidence types.
Missing-evidence requests and applicant calls are conditional; their shares are averaged across applications.
Supplementary evidence repeats the same extraction and validation controls before use.
Extraction does not generate a credit score or make an approval or rejection decision.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
Consent and access work includes GDPR assessment, document-processing permissions and consultation screening; required national procedures may extend elapsed delivery time.
unknowns: Which loan products and applicant groups are actually handled?
What share of evidence arrives as structured fields versus documents?
Which repayment calculations and evidence requirements are approved?
Can the lending records system accept reviewed fields with source references?
What privacy, retention, national lending and employee consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Which extraction errors could materially change a repayment assessment?
Which evidence types require independent verification rather than document reading?
Can an approved checklist identify gaps before applicants submit a formal application?
new_work: Review material extracted fields and resolve conflicting evidence.
Maintain evidence requirements and calculation rules.
Monitor extraction failures across document types and languages.
Maintain the applicant readiness checklist.
Investigate authenticity concerns and preserve the evidence trail.
tasks.statement: Examine, evaluate, or process loan applications.

tasks.short: Approve or reject credit facilities and loans within delegated lending authority.

steps.what: Retrieve the validated application, credit assessment and existing exposure.
Review repayment prospects, security, policy exceptions and proposed terms.
Route the recommendation to the required approval level.
Discuss material risks, exceptions and conditions where committee review is required.
Approve, reject or defer the facility and record reasons and conditions.
Send the approved decision notice and record delivery.

tasks.design: Configure the lending records system in {OTHER} and {WORKFLOW} to assemble decision packs, route by delegated authority and record decisions. Human approvers assess credit and approve the exact notice; {EMAIL} sends only that approved version to a verified recipient and records delivery.
tasks.previous_blocker: Approval limits, exceptions and committee records were scattered across documents and mail. The financial decision itself was often treated as inseparable from its administrative routing.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned approval rules, structured decision records and existing workflow configuration can handle routing and paperwork. No model is required for this design.
tasks.still_hard: Credit judgement, security enforceability and concentration risk remain substantive work. GDPR, the EU AI Act and national lending rules require scope-specific assessment, particularly for natural-person creditworthiness.
tasks.human_edge: Taking responsibility for uncertain repayment prospects and weighing an exception against portfolio risk.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time chasing approvals and more time assessing unusual exposures and conditions. Lending limits and formal decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Assess borrower repayment capacity.
reach.learn: Debt-service analysis, security quality and evidence-based credit reasoning.

reach.task: Review portfolio concentrations.
reach.learn: Connected exposures, sector concentration and stress losses.

evidence.claim: Delegated-authority routing, versioned approval records and approved-template notifications can be configured deterministically.
Significant decisions about natural persons require assessment under GDPR Article 22; meaningful human review cannot be a rubber stamp.
Natural-person creditworthiness assessment can fall within the EU AI Act's high-risk scope.

assumptions: This lending task applies to a mid-size lender or a company with a genuine lending activity; it is usually absent from ordinary corporate finance.
The loan origination or servicing system is represented by {OTHER}.
Shares represent a mixed caseload; committee review is conditional and its time is averaged across cases.
The originating credit assessment is supplied by the application-processing task rather than repeated here.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
Access estimates include legal and consultation screening; required procedures under national rules may extend elapsed delivery time.
unknowns: Does the company lend, and which loan or credit products are in scope?
Which decisions need individual, dual or committee approval?
Can the lending records system enforce authority limits and approved-notice versions?
Are applicants businesses, natural persons or both?
Which national lending and employee consultation rules apply?
research_questions: Can every approval route be expressed as an auditable decision table?
Which conditions must block notice release or later disbursement?
new_work: Maintain authority limits and approval substitutions.
Investigate stalled or incorrectly routed decisions.
Audit that notices match approved decisions and recipients.
Review access rights and decision-record completeness.
tasks.statement: Approve, reject, or coordinate the approval or rejection of lines of credit or commercial, real estate, or personal loans.

tasks.short: Monitor liquidity, forecast cash needs, and oversee authorised movements of funds.

steps.what: Check balances and recent movements in the {BANK}.
Check receivables, payables, and planned disbursements in the {ERP}.
Reconcile balances and expected movements in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Update the cash forecast and scenarios in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Decide funding, payment priorities, and transfers against liquidity limits.
Prepare payment or transfer instructions in the {BANK}.
Check and authorise release of instructions in the {BANK}.

tasks.design: Scheduled integrations bring {BANK} and {ERP} data into the {DATA_PLATFORM}, where deterministic reconciliation and scenario calculations feed a {BI} liquidity dashboard. The finance manager chooses cash actions, and configured {BANK} controls require authorised signatories before funds move.
tasks.previous_blocker: Bank formats, forecast assumptions, and payment calendars differ. Reliable reconciliation and secure access cost more than the forecast calculation itself.
tasks.enabler_now: Bank feeds, finance exports, and existing approval controls support a practical build. AI-assisted coding can accelerate adapters and validation rules without replacing treasury judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Receipt timing, restricted cash, currency exposure, and sudden funding needs remain uncertain. Payment release requires strong segregation of duties.
tasks.human_edge: Balancing liquidity resilience, supplier relationships, financing costs, and commercial priorities.

ambition.what: A daily downside-liquidity review using delayed-receipt scenarios.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling cash positions to challenging assumptions and choosing responses earlier. No new payment authority is granted by the automation.

reach.task: Manage short-term funding and liquidity buffers.
reach.learn: Learn funding lead times, covenant headroom, and treasury controls.

reach.task: Assess liquidity under adverse receipt and currency scenarios.
reach.learn: Learn stress assumptions and exposure limits.

evidence.claim: Nomentia supports cash forecasting using bank and finance data and forecast-versus-actual comparison.
Reconciliation, scenario arithmetic, and approval routing can be deterministic; funding decisions retain human judgement.

assumptions: The task concerns corporate treasury rather than securities trading or fund management.
A spreadsheet currently joins bank positions, expected movements, and forecast assumptions.
Time shares represent the end-to-end oversight task, including treasury support and signatory checks.
Build ranges are pilot estimates, not measured delivery results.
unknowns: Bank feed availability, security requirements, and charges.
Whether existing software already provides suitable forecasting.
Currencies, accounts, cash restrictions, and intercompany arrangements.
Signatory rules and whether the finance manager is an authorised signatory.
Access lead times and any applicable consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which reconciliation exceptions require judgement rather than better matching rules?
Would configuring existing forecasting be cheaper than building the proposed calculations?
new_work: Resolve stale feeds and unmatched cash movements.
Maintain receipt assumptions, scenario parameters, and liquidity limits.
Monitor access controls and retain approval evidence.
tasks.statement: Oversee the flow of cash or financial instruments.

tasks.short: Prepare, approve and release financial reports for regulators and the board.

steps.what: Confirm reporting requirements, deadlines, scope and material judgements.
Retrieve closed balances, reconciliations and supporting schedules.
Map balances into report schedules and check totals and comparatives.
Investigate validation exceptions and document accounting treatments.
Assemble the report and write disclosures and financial commentary.

loop.input: Validated schedules, required disclosure checklist, approved accounting notes and report template.
loop.output: Draft narrative sections with references to schedule rows and accounting notes.
loop.check: Validate amounts deterministically and check disclosure coverage; an analyst reviews interpretation and wording.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per section; missing evidence produces a flagged gap.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables and fixed wording use templates; variable explanations require reading accounting notes.

steps.what: Approve the exact report version, destination and release timing.
Submit approved filings or distribute approved board packs.
Archive the released report, supporting evidence and delivery receipt.

tasks.design: A deterministic generator on the {DATA_PLATFORM} maps closed {ERP} balances into validated schedules and report templates in {DOCS}. A bounded loop drafts variable narrative from approved accounting notes, while {WORKFLOW} records sign-off on the exact report and release destination. Supported interfaces deliver approved filings through {GOV_PORTAL} or board packs through {DOCS}, then archive receipts and source references.
tasks.previous_blocker: Report layouts, account mappings and supporting evidence were maintained separately. Automation was brittle when requirements or accounting treatments changed.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned mappings, reusable report templates and automated validation reduce repeated assembly. Faster coding lowers the cost of maintaining a narrow reporting generator.
tasks.still_hard: Material accounting judgements and changing reporting requirements need expert interpretation. Unsupported filing interfaces retain a manual submission step, and automation cannot substitute for the required signatory.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining material uncertainty, choosing defensible accounting treatments and accepting responsibility for the released report.

ambition.what: A board reporting pack with a source trail for every reported financial amount.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends more time on material disclosures and board questions, with less report assembly and evidence chasing. Statutory and board approval rights remain with existing signatories.

reach.task: Prepare supporting schedules and accounting disclosures.
reach.learn: Reporting mappings, close controls and materiality.

reach.task: Maintain governed reporting datasets.
reach.learn: Data lineage, versioned definitions and access controls.

evidence.claim: Financial report tables, cross-checks and source indexes can be generated with deterministic mappings and templates.
Variable reporting narrative can be drafted from approved notes, but disclosure completeness and accounting judgement need human review.

assumptions: The first release covers one report family, one reporting perimeter and established accounting policies.
Shares average the applicable release branch; a report is not necessarily both filed and sent to the board.
The filing automation estimate assumes a supported submission interface; otherwise submission stays manual.
The authorised report signatory reviews and approves the release in step s6.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
Access work includes confidential-data controls, GDPR screening and consultation screening under national rules.
unknowns: Which reports, jurisdictions and signatories are in scope?
Are source balances closed and supporting schedules reconciled?
Which filing destinations support automated submission and reliable receipts?
What evidence retention and access requirements apply?
Does the proposed data use require employee consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Which validation failures would prevent an incorrect but internally balanced report?
Can each material disclosure be linked to an approved evidence record?
new_work: Maintain reporting templates, mappings and disclosure checklists.
Review narrative and investigate validation exceptions.
Test changed reporting requirements against prior reports.
Monitor submissions and resolve missing or rejected receipts.
tasks.statement: Prepare financial or regulatory reports required by laws, regulations, or boards of directors.

tasks.short: Assess financial health and future performance using financial records, forecasts and operating assumptions.

steps.what: Retrieve financial balances, cash positions and operating forecasts.
Reconcile extracts and align periods, currencies and account mappings.
Examine profitability, liquidity, working capital and forecast deviations.
Model scenarios and select assumptions worth challenging.
Challenge operating assumptions and agree plausible responses.
Write the financial assessment and explain material changes.

loop.input: Validated scenario tables, agreed assumptions and recorded management explanations.
loop.output: Draft financial assessment with references to table cells and assumption records.
loop.check: Check every amount against calculated tables; flag unsupported explanations for analyst review.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per assessment; unresolved claims become blanks for the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle figures, but explanations vary with free-text operating context.

steps.what: Approve the financial outlook and recommend management action.

tasks.design: Scheduled integrations reconcile {ERP}, {BANK} and {CRM} data in the {DATA_PLATFORM}, then feed financial indicators and deterministic scenarios into {BI}. A bounded drafting loop prepares commentary in {DOCS} from validated figures and recorded explanations; the finance manager approves the outlook and recommendations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Account mappings, forecast definitions and spreadsheet models differed between teams. Maintaining integrations often cost more than each reporting cycle justified.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting configuration and faster integration development reduce setup effort. A bounded model loop can draft explanations without calculating financial results.
tasks.still_hard: Forecasts depend on uncertain demand, payment behaviour and management responses. Reliable data lineage and confidential access remain necessary.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when historical patterns no longer apply and challenging optimistic assumptions without losing business cooperation.

ambition.what: A weekly downside-liquidity review with named intervention triggers.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling figures to testing scenarios and challenging business assumptions. The manager can refresh scenarios within the planning remit; formal investment and financing approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Maintain driver-based forecasts.
reach.learn: Driver selection, sensitivity analysis and forecast backtesting.

reach.task: Assess short-term liquidity headroom.
reach.learn: Cash timing, facility availability and liquidity buffers.

evidence.claim: Bank and finance data can support cash forecasts and comparisons against actuals; this supports the cash component only.
Reconciliation, financial ratios and scenario calculations can use deterministic rules; selecting assumptions remains judgement.

assumptions: The initial scope covers one reporting perimeter and a limited set of financial scenarios.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.
The consent and access range covers permissions and consultation screening; formal consultation under national rules may extend elapsed delivery time.
unknowns: Which systems provide usable exports or interfaces?
Are account mappings, exchange-rate conventions and forecast definitions agreed?
How much reconciliation and scenario preparation time does the manager actually spend?
Will any proposed data use trigger employee consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Which indicators give actionable warning before cash or margin deteriorates?
Can historical forecasts be reconstructed well enough to test scenario quality?
new_work: Resolve reconciliation exceptions and maintain mappings.
Review drafted explanations against source figures.
Backtest forecasts and retire misleading indicators.
Maintain access permissions and integration alerts.
tasks.statement: Develop or analyze information to assess the current or future financial status of firms.

tasks.short: Prepare financial information, brief owners or investors, and discuss funding needs.

steps.what: Collect financial actuals, approved forecasts, and funding requirements.
Reconcile headline metrics and calculate funding scenarios.
Draft the financial briefing and responses to expected investor questions.

loop.input: Reconciled metrics, funding scenarios, existing investor questions, and disclosure policy.
loop.output: Draft briefing with source-linked commentary and proposed question responses.
loop.check: Insert figures deterministically; validate references and calculation consistency; the manager checks claims and disclosure boundaries.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per briefing; unsupported claims and unanswered questions return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Explaining results and addressing varied investor concerns requires free-text drafting.

steps.what: Approve the briefing's claims and permitted disclosures.
Send the approved briefing to authorised recipients.
Explain results, discuss funding needs, and answer investor concerns.
Record open questions and assign follow-up actions.

loop.input: Written meeting notes and recorded follow-up commitments.
loop.output: Draft question log and action list with proposed owners and deadlines.
loop.check: Link actions to note passages; the manager confirms commitments, owners, and dates.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per meeting; ambiguous commitments remain unassigned.
loop.why_not_simpler: Questions and commitments are expressed in varied meeting notes.

tasks.design: Configured exports from the {ERP} feed deterministic metric checks and funding tables on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A bounded loop drafts source-linked briefings in the {DOCS}; the {WORKFLOW} records disclosure approval and recipient confirmation before distribution through the {EMAIL}, then prepares follow-up records from meeting notes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Metrics, forecasts, narrative explanations, and recipient permissions were maintained separately. External communications also require judgement about disclosure and commitments.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic metric validation and bounded drafting can share a controlled dataset. Existing approval and distribution functions provide explicit release points.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, selective disclosure, uncertain forecasts, and funding negotiations remain human responsibilities.
tasks.human_edge: Read investor concerns, explain uncertainty honestly, and negotiate without making premature commitments.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time building packs and more time preparing funding options and meeting owners. The change grants no authority to accept financing terms or disclose additional information.

reach.task: Compare funding scenarios and investor return implications.
reach.learn: Learn financing structures, dilution, sensitivity analysis, and valuation assumptions.

reach.task: Translate liquidity forecasts into funding requirements.
reach.learn: Learn cash timing, covenant headroom, and financing lead times.

evidence.claim: Deterministic metric checks and template generation can automate much of financial briefing preparation.
Bounded drafting can prepare commentary and follow-up records while people retain disclosure and negotiation decisions.

assumptions: The typical company is privately held and communicates with owners or a limited investor group.
Funding discussions do not themselves authorise binding financing commitments.
Distribution approval includes checking the final attachment and recipient list; its time is counted in human review and approval steps.
Step shares and build ranges are estimates for one recurring briefing format.
EU GDPR applies to personal contact data; EU AI Act applicability depends on the implemented use. Disclosure and consultation duties also depend on national rules.
unknowns: Ownership structure and whether listed-company disclosure duties apply.
Who approves financial claims, recipients, and financing commitments.
Whether forecasts and metric definitions are already reconciled.
Which investor materials and notes may enter the drafting environment.
research_questions: Which recurring investor questions can be answered from approved figures?
Which disclosures require additional legal or executive review?
Can existing reporting templates eliminate narrative drafting for routine updates?
new_work: Review draft claims and source references.
Confirm recipients and final release versions.
Resolve ambiguous questions and follow-up commitments.
Maintain metric definitions and disclosure templates.
tasks.statement: Communicate with stockholders or other investors to provide information or to raise capital.

tasks.short: Evaluate financial systems and controls, compare improvements, and recommend changes.

steps.what: Gather transaction extracts, control logs, and current procedures.
Reconcile extracts and calculate processing times, errors, and control exceptions.
Explain exceptions, workarounds, and practical constraints.
Compare change costs, expected benefits, and control coverage.
Select a recommendation and assess its operational and financial tradeoffs.
Write the recommendation, supporting evidence, costs, and proposed implementation plan.

loop.input: Preferred option, calculated comparison, and evidence with record references.
loop.output: Change proposal with referenced claims and explicit assumptions.
loop.check: Validate figures against calculated tables; financial manager checks recommendations and unsupported claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair; missing evidence produces marked gaps and a template fallback.
loop.why_not_simpler: The proposal must explain varied process constraints and tradeoffs in prose.

steps.what: Approve, amend, or reject the proposed change and funding.

tasks.design: Configure exports from the {ERP} and evidence access in {DOCS}, then reconcile them on the {DATA_PLATFORM} into a control baseline in {BI}. A deterministic comparison tool calculates scenarios, and a bounded drafting loop prepares the proposal from the manager's chosen option. Approval in {WORKFLOW} records the finance director's decision before funding or control changes take effect.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence gathering crossed systems, and local control definitions made reusable comparisons expensive to build.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports and approval features cover much of the plumbing. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building reconciliation rules and scenario templates.
tasks.still_hard: Estimating adoption costs, detecting weak evidence, and judging whether a control change shifts risk elsewhere remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: The manager tests explanations, challenges optimistic assumptions, and balances control strength against operating friction.

ambition.what: Monthly selection of one measured finance-control improvement for a limited pilot.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into evidence assembly and proposal formatting; more goes into testing options with process owners. The manager can sponsor pilots within existing delegated limits; spending and policy approval rights do not automatically change.

reach.task: Define reliable control-performance measures across finance processes.
reach.learn: Data lineage, metric definitions, and reconciliation tests.

reach.task: Design a control test for a proposed process change.
reach.learn: Control objectives, sampling, and evidence sufficiency.

evidence.claim: Structured finance extracts support deterministic reconciliations, baseline measures, and scenario calculations.
A bounded drafting loop can assemble an evidence-linked proposal, while option selection remains managerial judgement.

assumptions: This concerns a corporate finance department rather than investment-fund management.
Time shares are planning estimates, informed by the supplied priors.
The first release covers one process and uses existing reporting access.
Consent and access estimates include any applicable employee consultation under national rules; formal procedures may extend elapsed time.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply as relevant; the design does not introduce individual employee scoring.
unknowns: Which process is the first review target?
Are transaction timestamps and control failures recorded consistently?
What pilot budget and approval limits already exist?
Do proposed metrics identify employees and trigger consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Can current reporting configuration produce the baseline without custom code?
Which proposed measures predict a meaningful improvement rather than a reporting change?
new_work: Maintain metric definitions and reconciliation rules.
Review proposal claims and change estimates.
Investigate missing evidence and measure pilot outcomes.
tasks.statement: Evaluate financial reporting systems, accounting or collection procedures, or investment activities and make recommendations for changes to procedures, operating systems, budgets, or other financial control functions.

tasks.short: Build community relationships that create qualified business introductions.

steps.what: Choose relevant community events and contacts using relationship history.
Read contact background and prepare relevant conversation topics.

loop.input: Selected contacts, permitted relationship notes, and supplied public background.
loop.output: Short meeting brief with sources and possible conversation topics.
loop.check: Require a source for each factual claim; manager checks relevance and sensitivity.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair per brief; omit unsupported facts and fall back to contact history.
loop.why_not_simpler: Relevant context is spread across varied free-text notes and background documents.

steps.what: Exchange availability and arrange selected meetings.
Meet contacts, understand needs, and build trust through conversation.
Record useful relationship context and agreed follow-up actions.

loop.output: Proposed contact update and follow-up tasks.
loop.check: Show each field beside its source note; manager confirms facts and permitted retention.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction; ambiguous details remain blank for manual entry.
loop.why_not_simpler: Brief conversation notes do not follow a stable field structure.

steps.what: Send a personal follow-up or make the agreed introduction.

tasks.design: Use the {CRM} and {CALENDAR} to support contact selection and routine scheduling for manager-selected contacts. Bounded loops prepare sourced briefs and turn the manager's notes into proposed {CRM} updates. The manager holds conversations and sends personal introductions, with reminders configured in {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: The valuable work depended on trust, while preparation and record keeping were scattered across notes and correspondence.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling and contact-management configuration handles coordination. Small text loops can reduce preparation and note-entry work.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, discretion, timing, and credible introductions remain personal. Sparse records can make preparation misleading.
tasks.human_edge: The manager notices unspoken concerns, judges mutual fit, and puts personal credibility behind an introduction.

ambition.what: A quarterly introductory finance session for first-time local business owners.

tasks.altitude: Most of the week still involves people; preparation and follow-up administration shrink modestly. No new commercial commitment or pricing authority is gained.

reach.task: Recognise when an introduction needs an initial financial suitability review.
reach.learn: Basic credit indicators and the boundary between an introduction and a credit assessment.

evidence.claim: Contact records, reminders, and calendar configuration can reduce networking administration.
Text preparation can support networking, but relationship formation and introductions remain strongly human.

assumptions: This task applies to a financial manager with an explicit external business-development remit; it is not universal in corporate finance.
Scheduling is limited to selected contacts, standard invitations, and permitted availability.
Conversation notes are entered by the manager; recording meetings is outside scope.
Contact processing follows GDPR, retention rules, and applicable national communication rules.
Employee consultation under national rules is assessed if the implementation changes workplace monitoring.
unknowns: Does the role actually have a business-development remit?
Which contacts may be retained and approached?
Are shared contact records available and current?
What kinds of introductions may the manager make?
research_questions: Can existing contact forms and templates make structured note entry easier than a model loop?
Does a brief improve conversation preparation enough to justify its review time?
new_work: Check briefs for stale or unsupported background.
Confirm extracted contact updates and retention relevance.
Maintain scheduling limits and remove obsolete follow-up tasks.
tasks.statement: Network within communities to find and attract new business.

tasks.short: Review collection status, reconcile outstanding balances, and identify accounts needing attention.

steps.what: Retrieve the receivables ageing and recent collection activity.
Reconcile outstanding balances against receipts, credits, and ledger totals.
Read the collection report and total overdue, disputed, and promised amounts.
Read collector explanations to clarify unresolved statuses and payment promises.

loop.input: Collector explanations linked to customer and invoice references.
loop.output: Proposed dispute status, promise date, amount, and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Require matching invoice references and quoted evidence; validate dates and amounts against the ledger.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per batch; ambiguous or conflicting messages remain unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text explanations contain conditional promises and dispute details absent from structured records.

steps.what: Confirm material exceptions and decide which accounts need investigation.
Record investigation priorities and assign internal follow-up.

tasks.design: Configure ageing and collection views in the {ERP}, with deterministic reconciliation on the {DATA_PLATFORM} where receipts and credits need additional matching. A bounded loop turns collector messages from {EMAIL} into evidence-linked status proposals beside the collection summary in {BI}. The manager confirms material exceptions before the {ERP} creates internal follow-up tasks; this workflow does not authorise write-offs or customer demands.
tasks.previous_blocker: Receipt timing, invoice references, and collector notes did not align cleanly with the report being reviewed.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing receivables features cover ageing and totals. Small reconciliation adapters and bounded extraction can bridge remaining gaps.
tasks.still_hard: Unallocated cash, partial settlements, disputed invoices, and conditional payment promises can remain ambiguous.
tasks.human_edge: The manager distinguishes a reporting mismatch from a genuine collection problem and judges which uncertainty deserves attention.

ambition.what: Daily prioritisation of high-value disputed receivables for investigation.

tasks.altitude: Routine balance reading becomes an exception review, leaving more time to resolve disputed or unclear accounts. Credit limits, settlement terms, and write-off authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Turn an ambiguous payment promise into a documented follow-up plan.
reach.learn: Dispute categories, promise evidence, and appropriate escalation.

reach.task: Identify when worsening arrears warrant a credit review.
reach.learn: Exposure aggregation, payment patterns, and credit-review triggers.

evidence.claim: Ageing buckets, balance totals, receipt matching, and internal follow-up routing are largely rule-based finance functions.
Free-text payment promises require contextual extraction and confirmation before changing collection status.

assumptions: A spreadsheet currently bridges report snapshots and receipt or credit details; companies with integrated views can eliminate that step.
Structured statuses are used directly; text extraction is limited to unresolved exceptions.
No automated customer contact, credit decision, settlement, or write-off is included.
GDPR applies where accounts or messages identify individuals; access is limited to collection purposes.
Consultation under national rules is assessed if activity reporting becomes employee monitoring.
unknowns: Does the existing receivables configuration already reconcile receipts and credits?
How current are collection statuses and payment allocations?
Are invoice references present in collector messages?
Which balances and disputes are material?
Who may confirm statuses and assign investigations?
research_questions: Can configuring existing receivables views eliminate the separate report and reconciliation workbook?
Which matching rules safely handle partial payments and credit notes?
Would structured collector fields remove the need for text extraction?
new_work: Investigate unmatched receipts and inconsistent credits.
Confirm ambiguous status proposals.
Maintain materiality thresholds and matching rules.
Check that assigned follow-up tasks are resolved.
tasks.statement: Review collection reports to determine the status of collections and the amounts of outstanding balances.

tasks.short: Define and implement safeguards for financial assets, records, and borrowing collateral.

steps.what: Collect asset records, access lists, and bank mandates.
Compare existing safeguards with contracts, mandates, and retention requirements.

loop.input: Applicable loan agreements, mandates, retention requirements, and control procedures.
loop.output: Cited obligations and candidate gaps against custody evidence.
loop.check: Check each obligation against its source passage; the manager validates applicability and claimed gaps.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per document; missing or conflicting evidence goes to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Contract obligations and procedural exceptions appear in varied free-text documents.

steps.what: Agree custody responsibilities, segregation of duties, and acceptable residual risks.
Write custody procedures, escalation routes, and evidence requirements.

loop.input: Control decisions, validated obligations, and the approved procedure template.
loop.output: Draft custody procedures linked to decisions and supporting evidence.
loop.check: Require owners, evidence, escalation routes, and source references; the manager checks operational feasibility.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per procedure; unresolved decisions remain visibly open.
loop.why_not_simpler: The procedure must express case-specific responsibilities and exceptions in readable instructions.

steps.what: Approve custody procedures and accepted residual risks.
Configure access and approval controls, then validate their operation.
Review control failures and assign corrective actions.

tasks.design: Read custody evidence from the {ERP}, {BANK}, and {CLM} into a controlled register on the {WORKFLOW}. Bounded loops prepare cited gap lists and procedures in the {DOCS}; approved controls use existing {ERP} permissions and approval settings, with exceptions shown in the {BI}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence crossed systems and legal documents, while control ownership and exceptions were inconsistently recorded.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic evidence collection and existing permission settings cover much of the implementation. Bounded extraction and drafting reduce document work while keeping control decisions explicit.
tasks.still_hard: Legacy permissions, physical custody, conflicting contractual duties, and effective segregation in small teams remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: Design controls that people can follow and detect when formal compliance hides practical exposure.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time collecting evidence and rewriting procedures, and more time testing whether safeguards work. Risk acceptance and changes to financial authority retain their existing approval routes.

reach.task: Test custody controls and trace supporting evidence.
reach.learn: Learn control sampling, evidence sufficiency, and segregation-of-duties testing.

reach.task: Review bank mandates and collateral obligations.
reach.learn: Learn banking authority structures, collateral restrictions, and mandate change procedures.

evidence.claim: Permission configuration, approval rules, evidence registers, and exception reporting support financial custody controls.
Free-text contractual obligations can be extracted into cited drafts for human validation.

assumptions: The company mainly safeguards operating assets, bank authority, and financial records.
Collateral procedures apply only where borrowing creates relevant obligations; investment custody is not assumed.
Step shares and build ranges are estimates for a limited initial control scope.
EU GDPR applies where evidence identifies people; EU AI Act applicability depends on use.
Consultation for access monitoring follows national rules. The access range includes consultation effort where applicable, not guaranteed elapsed approval time.
unknowns: Which assets, securities, and collateral the company actually holds.
Whether access evidence can be exported from the {ERP} and {BANK}.
The current control approval matrix and permitted segregation exceptions.
Whether proposed evidence collection introduces employee monitoring.
research_questions: Which safeguards can be enforced through existing system settings?
Which controls need physical inspection or independent verification?
new_work: Validate extracted obligations and draft procedures.
Maintain control ownership and evidence links.
Investigate control failures and stale access records.
Retest controls after permission or process changes.
tasks.statement: Establish procedures for custody or control of assets, records, loan collateral, or securities to ensure safekeeping.

tasks.short: Review securities transactions and prices to assess market conditions affecting treasury holdings.

steps.what: Retrieve securities transaction reports from the {BANK}.
Collect dated price lists from the market-data service {OTHER}, stored in the {DOCS}.
Match instruments and calculate price movements, yields and exposures in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Assess market movements against liquidity needs, investment limits and holding-specific risks.
Record the market assessment and follow-up recommendations in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Manager's market assessment, validated market comparison and investment policy excerpts.
loop.output: Draft market review note with source references and proposed follow-up.
loop.check: Check every figure against calculation records; manager checks interpretation and recommendations.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass, capped at two model calls; unresolved claims return to manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template handles tables, but expressing case-specific reasoning from the manager's assessment needs flexible writing.

tasks.design: Configure scheduled securities reports from the {BANK} and licensed price exports from the market-data service {OTHER}. A job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} validates identifiers, dates and currencies, calculates comparisons, and feeds a {BI} view with exceptions. A bounded drafting loop combines validated figures with the manager's assessment; the manager approves the review note before it is filed in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different instrument identifiers, price conventions and report formats made recurring reconciliation expensive. Market interpretation still required judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports and scheduled feeds can supply structured records. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building mappings, calculations and document assembly; no forecasting breakthrough is assumed.
tasks.still_hard: Licensed data, illiquid instruments, stale quotes and corporate actions need care. Explaining whether a price movement matters to this company's liquidity remains judgement-heavy.
tasks.human_edge: The manager connects market evidence to upcoming cash needs, risk tolerance and uncertainty, and challenges misleading comparisons.

ambition.what: Weekly review of whether short-term investment maturities still match upcoming cash obligations.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from collecting prices and rebuilding comparisons to investigating exceptions and assessing liquidity implications. The manager gains earlier opportunities to recommend maturity changes; trading authority does not change.

reach.task: Assess interest-rate and counterparty exposure under adverse scenarios.
reach.learn: Duration, concentration limits, scenario construction and the limits of quoted prices.

evidence.claim: Scheduled imports, identifier matching and financial calculations can automate preparation while interpretation remains human.
This securities-review task applies mainly where a company holds treasury investments; many mid-size companies have little such work.
The proposed build ranges and remaining-time percentages are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: Scope is the company's own treasury holdings, rather than managing investments for clients.
The task recurs often enough to justify scheduled preparation.
The bank and market-data service offer usable exports under suitable licences.
Calculations use approved conventions for currency, accrued interest and reporting dates.
Build ranges cover one bank connection and one market-data feed.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply where relevant. National rules determine employee consultation obligations; consultation time is included if required.
unknowns: Whether the company holds securities and how often these reviews occur.
Instrument types, custody accounts, transaction volume and valuation conventions.
Available exports, feed licences, integration permissions and data charges.
Current division of preparation and review between finance staff and the manager.
Existing investment limits and delegated decision rights.
Whether employee consultation is required under applicable national rules.
research_questions: Can existing reporting configuration provide complete transactions and dated prices?
Which instrument identifiers and corporate actions require explicit reconciliation rules?
Which comparisons materially inform treasury decisions rather than repeat available reports?
What historical cases should validate stale-price detection and yield calculations?
new_work: Resolve missing identifiers, stale prices and unmatched transactions.
Maintain calculation conventions and instrument mappings.
Review draft notes for unsupported explanations and recommendations.
Monitor feed failures, access permissions and licence renewals.
tasks.statement: Review reports of securities transactions or price lists to analyze market conditions.

role_batches.altitude: The finance manager spends less time reconstructing records and coordinating paperwork, and more time on liquidity choices, customer resolutions, coaching, and hiring. Better visibility supports earlier decisions; additional financial or employment authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: Treasurers and Controllers: short-term funding and liquidity buffers.
Credit Analysts: customer exposure and payment-term decisions.
Budget Analysts: capacity and staffing-cost scenarios.
Business Intelligence Analysts: reliable process metrics.
Compliance Officers: financial controls and personal-data use.
skills_to_grow: Define reconciliation rules and useful exception thresholds.
Challenge cash assumptions and interpret stress scenarios.
Review sourced summaries and detect unsupported commitments.
Design fair work examples and record hiring evidence.
Understand access controls, GDPR, the EU AI Act, and applicable national consultation rules.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Run an early-warning finance service that connects liquidity stress, customer payment difficulties, and team bottlenecks to timely human decisions.

role_batches.altitude: The financial manager's week shifts toward cost tradeoffs, coaching, control effectiveness, and funding conversations. Financial approval, employment decisions, and external commitments retain their existing delegated limits.
reach: Work with budget analysts on driver-based scenarios.
Work with controllers and auditors on evidence-based control testing.
Work with treasurers and financial analysts on liquidity and funding options.
skills_to_grow: Control design and segregation of duties
role_batches.ambitious_version: Offer a recurring financial decision service: monthly spending options, practical close clinics, bank-mandate exposure reviews, and quarterly owner liquidity briefings, using shared reconciled data and explicit approval limits.

role_batches.altitude: The finance manager's week shifts toward financial interpretation, scenario challenge and accountable approval. Better preparation supports faster investigation and discussion; formal reporting, financing and lending authorities remain with their designated holders.
reach: Budget analyst: driver-based forecasting and forecast backtesting.
Treasurer: liquidity headroom and cash timing.
Accountant: reporting controls, accounting judgements and disclosure evidence.
Credit analyst: repayment capacity and defensible credit recommendations, where lending applies.
skills_to_grow: Define financial metrics, mappings and validation rules.
Test scenarios and distinguish calculated outputs from uncertain assumptions.
Review sourced model outputs and investigate exceptions.
Maintain approval controls, data lineage and confidential access.
Communicate material uncertainty and challenge business assumptions.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Run a weekly financial resilience review with traceable figures, downside scenarios and explicit intervention triggers, while offering the board source-linked reporting. Where the company lends, add applicant evidence-readiness support and consistent credit packs under existing approval authority.

role_batches.altitude: The financial manager spends less time assembling evidence and more time challenging explanations, testing improvements, and resolving material exceptions. Decision rights expand only through explicit delegation; better reporting alone does not confer spending, credit, or policy authority.
reach: Business intelligence analyst: define traceable finance measures and reporting datasets.
Accountant and auditor: design evidence-based tests of control changes.
Financial risk specialist: translate emerging indicators into escalation decisions.
Credit analyst: connect collection exceptions with credit-review needs.
skills_to_grow: Data access, retention, and applicable consultation requirements
role_batches.ambitious_version: Run a weekly finance exception clinic that joins liquidity, collections, and operating-risk evidence, then proposes a focused investigation or limited control pilot within existing approval limits.

role_batches.altitude: For this task, the financial manager spends more time assessing treasury exposure and less time assembling evidence. Existing investment approval rights remain in place.
reach: Work with the treasurer on matching investment maturities to liquidity needs.
Work with the financial risk specialist on interest-rate and counterparty scenarios.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Run a weekly treasury exposure review that links market movements, maturity dates and upcoming cash obligations to specific recommendations.

summary.basis: 100 baseline hours; equal weight per loaded task; step shares normalized within each task
